chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does a man perform Hajj on behalf of the Naṣībī?' He said, 'No.' I said, 'And if it were his father?' He said, 'If it were his father, then yes.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And if a man takes a Ḥajjah (a specific person for whom he performs Hajj) and there is surplus [from the cost] from it, it is for him; and if he is unable [to complete it], it is upon him.'

key_terms.الشَّيْخُ: The Sheikh, referring to al-Shaykh al-Tusi, the compiler of the text
key_terms.النَّاصِبِ: Naṣībī, a specific rival or opponent, often referring to those who opposed the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.حَجَّةً: Ḥajjah, a specific person appointed to perform Hajj on behalf of another

ai.seo_question: Can a man perform Hajj on behalf of a Naṣībī or his father?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the validity of Hajj performed on behalf of a *Naṣībī* (rival of the Ahl al-Bayt), establishing a general prohibition that is lifted specifically for one's father, reflecting the high status of paternal rights in Shia jurisprudence. The concluding remark addresses the financial logistics of proxy Hajj, determining that surplus funds remain with the agent while any shortfall is the responsibility of the principal, ensuring clarity in ritual obligations.
